scenario_solution: Authored three vehicles on the real 874m Garching OpenDRIVE lane 160:0:-3. The route has no signal/stop controls and no parked-row occluders, so neither known blocker is suppressed. Cooperative shadow assumptions remain 8m/s intruder speed, 0.3s reaction and a 3s horizon. Sensing is explicitly upgraded from ego-only radial slabs to per-actor ideal visible boxes; hidden actors remain omitted. Reckless alpha alone uses the labelled 1s horizon and smaller clearance/stronger assumed braking envelope. Its surge choices close a real 95m initial lead distance; bravo reacts defensively and a native rear-end contact emerges. No contact, pose, or raw control was injected. The first near-miss threshold crossing is logged at approximately 13.1s; one contact event spans four observed overlap ticks, not four independent crashes. Following/yielding were demonstrated, not lane changing.

limits: Studio's headless Chrome lost its WebGL context. The real control-source toggle and server requests were exercised, but 3D visual confirmation of Studio motion is NOT claimed; native headless motion is separately measured.

Studio stops before unsupported signal/road-control or junction entries rather than assuming green. Arbitrary intersections, large off-road recovery, reverse takeover and lane changing are not qualified.

Bad-actor behavior ends with minimum-risk stopping after its feasible set disappears. There are real cloud calls throughout the 20s scene, but a stopped driver with no feasible alternatives does not buy meaningless model requests.
The runs are lockstep simulation with an explicitly ideal box sensor, not real-time road-safety validation. No public-road actuation, calibration study or general collision-proof guarantee.
No project-wide builds, tests, linters or formatters were run. Only targeted execution, schema checks, native/app smoke work, and the local package's editable installation were performed.
